statement: The literal identity is false for a general O_S-module M. For scalar torsor twists the valid functorial identity is (M^sharp)⊗2 ≅ (M⊗2)^b. With trivial torsors and M=O(1) on P¹_C the written formula would identify O(2) and O(1).
qualification: Refuted as written. R-C-SA16-502 gives (M^sharp)⊗2≅(M⊗2)^b. On P1_C with trivial torsors the literal formula equates degrees two and one.
attribution: Reconstruction/counterstatement of this run, not replacement transcript.

statement: For the invariant derivation Dδ with δ≠0 and canonical principal-part map pp_n:F_n/F_n−1≅t_E⊗n, gr_nDδ=−n·μδ. Multiplicatively rescaled symbols ε_n=c^n pp_n give −nc·μδ. No such convention makes every degree arrow coefficient1 while retaining Leibniz and multiplication.

statement: For a smooth elliptic curve over an algebraically closed field of odd characteristic p and δ≠0, ker(Dδ|F_n)={g^p:g∈F_floor(n/p)}. Its dimension is max(1,floor(n/p)); x^p for x of pole order2 first gives a nonconstant kernel element at2p. The manuscript’s unrestricted constant-kernel claim, and the reported modernization’s sufficient condition p∤n, fail.
qualification: R-C-SA16-519 gives the pth-power filtered kernel. For nonzero δ over an algebraically closed field of odd characteristic p, x^p∈F_(2p) is a nonconstant kernel element. It also belongs to F_(2p+1), refuting the proposed rescue p∤n.
attribution: Reconstruction/counterstatement of this run, not replacement transcript.

statement: For the Rees section ring R=⊕F_nT^n, extend D by D(fT^n)=D(f)T^(n+1). In characteristic0 its kernel is k[S] with S=1T. In characteristicp over a perfect field, ker D=R^p[S]. On the filtered union F∞ the kernels are instead k and F∞^p.

statement: For a dyadic DVR with uniformizerπ, unita=α²−b andb∈π²A, the tangent quadratic isX²+overline(2α/π)XY+overline(b/π²)Y². It is geometrically an ordinary node exactly whenv(2)=1. The unrestricted assertion fails forF2[[π]],a=1+π³ and forZ2[√2],a=5, whose tangent cones have a doubled line.

statement: ForP=εqQ the dyadic normality test must apply toP, not to the unsigned primitive factorQ. For exampleQ=1 is square mod4 whereasP=3 or−1 is not, and the corresponding dyadic quadratic order is normal. Later156 correctly writesεQ whenq=1.
